name: Sheen Green
lede: Sheen Green is a vivid yellow-green from the extended web color lists, its name describing a glossy finish on the base word "green" rather than naming a dye, place or coiner.

sections.title: A finish word, not a pedigree
sections.body:
Our library lists Sheen Green only as a Wikipedia-sourced crowd-list entry, with no dictionary, dye house or company credited and no first-recorded date [1]. "Sheen" names a surface quality, a soft gloss, the same way "satin" or "matte" would, so this is filed as a descriptive compound rather than a nature, place or person name [1]. Nothing in the sources checked here explains why this specific hex, rather than any other bright yellow-green, was picked to carry the word [1].

By our look-alike data the nearest color is [[slime-green|Slime Green]], 2.8 units away and read as almost the same, with [[apple-green|Apple Green]] further off at 4.4, also almost the same [2]. [[yellowish-green|Yellowish Green]] sits a little beyond that, 4.9 units off and read as lighter [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: At our matching threshold, this exact yellow-green does not turn up in any of the 23,781 paintings in the archive, as photographed [3]. That gap is typical of very saturated, high-chroma colors like this one, hue 121 degrees and chroma 90 out of roughly 100: period pigments rarely reached this vivid a green, and the absence is a gap in the match, not a claim about painting history generally [3]. Measured, it sits closer to a synthetic highlighter green than to any historical pigment green [3].
